drivingQuestion: Under what condition does collected meat residue impart the impurity of a carcass?
outcomeNote: A single amoraic gloss on the mishna's lemma, with no challenge or answer in this unit; it is challenged only later, in the following sugya.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָאָלָל [וְכוּ׳]. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְהוּא שֶׁכִּנְּסוֹ.
segments.en: §The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» With regard to «the meat residue» attached to the hide after flaying that was collected, if there is an olive-bulk of it in one place it imparts impurity of an animal carcass, and one who contracts impurity from it and eats consecrated foods or enters the Temple is liable to receive karet for it. «Rav Huna says» in explanation: This halakha «is» applicable only when a halakhically competent person «collected» the meat residue in one place, but not if the meat residue was collected by a child or without human intervention. By collecting it in one place, the person indicates that he considers it to be food.

moves.summary: the mishna's clause on R' Yehuda and collected meat residue is quoted as the lemma under discussion
moves.about: the mishna's clause that R' Yehuda holds collected meat residue of an olive-bulk imparts carcass impurity

moves.summary: Rav Huna restricts the ruling to residue a person deliberately collected
moves.about: R' Yehuda's ruling applies only where a person deliberately collected the meat residue in one place
